# Accordion

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use an accordion to let users reveal and hide related sections when showing all of the content at once would make a page difficult to scan.

## When to use

- Use for several related sections when users need only some of the content and can understand each section from its heading.
- Consider simplifying or splitting the page before introducing an accordion.
- Use expanded sections sparingly when a section is likely to be needed immediately.

## When not to use

- Do not hide information that most users need to complete the current task.
- Do not use an accordion as a substitute for a clear page structure or a sequence of service steps.
- Do not use it for content that users need to compare across sections at the same time.

## Anatomy

- **Accordion container (required):** A uniquely identified container carries govuk-accordion and data-module="govuk-accordion".
- **Section (required):** Each repeated section contains one header and one content region.
- **Section heading (required):** A heading at the correct document level contains the section-button hook and a unique ID.
- **Section content (required):** The content region has a unique ID associated with the same accordion and section position.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-accordion` | Related sections start collapsed after enhancement while remaining visible without JavaScript. |
| Expanded section | `div` | `govuk-accordion__section`, `govuk-accordion__section--expanded` | A section whose content should be open when the enhanced component first appears. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise the official govuk-accordion module from GOV.UK Frontend.
- Without JavaScript, all section content remains visible under ordinary headings.
- With JavaScript, GOV.UK Frontend creates disclosure controls, state text, and show-all behaviour.
- Container, heading, and content IDs must be unique on the page.

## Accessibility contract

- Choose heading elements that preserve the page's logical heading hierarchy.
- Section headings must identify the content clearly when read independently.
- Do not hand-build the enhanced button and ARIA state; initialise the official module from the documented base markup.
- Do not hide the unenhanced content before GOV.UK Frontend confirms JavaScript support.

## Content rules

- Use short, descriptive section headings.
- Place the information users need to decide whether to expand a section in its heading or optional summary.
- Avoid repeating the same opening words across every heading when distinctive wording is available.

## HTML examples

### Two-section accordion

```html
<div class="govuk-accordion" data-module="govuk-accordion" id="accordion-guidance">
  <div class="govuk-accordion__section">
    <div class="govuk-accordion__section-header">
      <h2 class="govuk-accordion__section-heading">
        <span class="govuk-accordion__section-button" id="accordion-guidance-heading-1">
          Writing well for the web
        </span>
      </h2>
    </div>
    <div id="accordion-guidance-content-1" class="govuk-accordion__section-content">
      <p class="govuk-body">This is the content for Writing well for the web.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="govuk-accordion__section">
    <div class="govuk-accordion__section-header">
      <h2 class="govuk-accordion__section-heading">
        <span class="govuk-accordion__section-button" id="accordion-guidance-heading-2">
          Know your audience
        </span>
      </h2>
    </div>
    <div id="accordion-guidance-content-2" class="govuk-accordion__section-content">
      <p class="govuk-body">This is the content for Know your audience.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</div>
```
